flags.observation: "JP Morgan sought software for rogue trading and failures" drops the card's "stop", inverting the claim: the bank now seeks rogue trading.
Line ends "with BMI, Commission." The card's core claim, that the Commission never looked into Ptech, is lost to a dangling noun.
Ends on the fragment "Pentagon bureaucracy, twenty-four hours." Without the catastrophe reference the timing point has no closure.
Reordered quote leaves "a long one." trailing after the catalyzing event; the line closes limp and the quote's sense blurs.
124 characters with the opener "Falsification has another author:"; not one breath, far beyond the 80-95 range and golden line lengths.
117 characters. Fourteen opener lines run 108 to 124 characters; the long narrator openers push every one past the spec range.
"Those figures reach:" leads into thirty-four killed bookkeepers, framing the dead as a ledger stop; "killed, office moved" ends anticlimactically.
"Those keys remain with:" repeats the opener family of "Those blueprints expose:" (beat 6) seven beats later; beat 23 repeats it again.
"The accounting wanders:" is an abstract bridge with no artworkPrompt image and no therefore-or-but logic linking it to Rumsfeld's war.
"That account commissions:" implies a causal link between Zakheim's company and the PNAC paper that neither card states; the phrase is opaque aloud.
The lore claim about Rumsfeld's war losing even more money is absent; the line recites power details "over a decade, no hearing".
Ledger scene sets a mood but never touches the deck title or kayfabe concept; the frame lacks satirical provocation aimed at money and power.
